hints.title: Customer Purchase Conditions
hints.text: Identify customers who purchased product A, purchased product B, and never purchased product C.

hints.title: Group-Level Boolean Aggregation
hints.text: Join Customers and Orders, then apply having sum(product_name = "A") > 0 and sum(product_name = "B") > 0 and sum(product_name = "C") = 0.

hints.title: Sorting Output
hints.text: order by customer_id ascending as specified in the schema specification.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM Customers c
JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name
HAVING SUM(o.product_name = 'A') > 0
   AND SUM(o.product_name = 'B') > 0
   AND SUM(o.product_name = 'C') = 0
ORDER BY c.customer_id;
```

complexity.notes: Group-by aggregation over orders filtered by HAVING conditions resolves in linear time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Multiple IN and NOT IN subqueries cause repeated scans across the entire Orders table.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Evaluating boolean sums in HAVING processes all conditions in a single group-by pass.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Single GROUP BY with boolean condition aggregation inside the HAVING clause.

solutions.code:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM Customers c
JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name
HAVING SUM(o.product_name = 'A') > 0
   AND SUM(o.product_name = 'B') > 0
   AND SUM(o.product_name = 'C') = 0
ORDER BY c.customer_id;

SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM Customers c
JOIN Orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN o.product_name = 'A' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN o.product_name = 'B' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0
   AND SUM(CASE WHEN o.product_name = 'C' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0
ORDER BY c.customer_id;
